features.name: Video export: H.264, H.265, AV1, VP9, APV in MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV
features.note: encoded by ffmpeg; hardware encoders are picked per OS (VideoToolbox, NVENC/QSV/AMF/MF); APV needs liboapv in the ffmpeg build. Windows: the installer ships the GPL FFmpeg build (libx264, libx265, libvpx, libsvtav1, libaom, libopus, libdav1d; nothing nonfree), and hardware encoders are still tried first. Checked 2026-11-04: H.264 MP4 in the installed app (h264_amf); AV1 MP4 (libsvtav1 and av1_amf), VP9 WebM with Opus, H.264 (libx264), HEVC MOV (libx265) and Ogg/Opus through the exporter with the shipped ffmpeg. av1_amf pads frames whose width is not a multiple of 64 or height not a multiple of 16 (720x1280 came out 768x1280), so it is used only for aligned sizes and SVT-AV1 takes the rest. AAC uses aac_mf at 192 kbps and below for constant bitrate like Android. macOS release builds bundle a GPL FFmpeg 9.0.2 with libx264, libx265, libvpx, libsvtav1, libopus and libdav1d: H.264 and H.265 use VideoToolbox up to 4096 px per side and libx264/libx265 above that, AV1 uses libsvtav1, VP9 libvpx-vp9 and Opus libopus (DeskExportTest checks H.264 MP4, HEVC MOV, AV1 MKV and VP9 WebM with Opus) Linux: DeskExportTest (H.264, HEVC, AV1, VP9 with sound) passes in Docker; an MP4 exported in clean Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 12 containers checked with the bundled ffprobe
